evidence.quote: Today the Federal Open Market Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point, bringing it to 1 to 1¼ percent.
additional gradual rate hikes are likely to be appropriate over the next few years to sustain the economic expansion.
Provided that the economy evolves broadly as the Committee anticipates, we currently expect to begin implementing a balance sheet normalization program this year.
Nonetheless, in light of the softer recent inflation readings, the Committee is monitoring inflation developments closely.
all of these indicators do signal a tight labor market.
The Committee believes we have conditions in place for inflation to move up, but that’s also a risk. And those things point, I think, to a gradual pace of reducing accommodation.

parsed.rationale: The Fed hiked, signaled further gradual increases, and laid out a plan to begin balance sheet runoff this year, all supported by a characterization of a tight labor market. Concern about soft inflation readings and an emphasis on gradualism temper the hawkish signal.
